SPECIFICATION FOR SILICONE COMPOUNDS FOR APPLICATION ON HIGH VOLTAGE PORCELAIN INSULATORS
0. FOREWO.RD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 18 April 1975, after the draft finalized by the Electrical Insulators and Accessories Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electrotechni,eal Division Council. 0.2 This specification deals with silicone compounds suitable for application either by hand or by brush or by sprayer on the surface of high voltage porcelain or glass insulators to prevent by their hydrophobic action tbc flashover of insulators due to pollution of the insulator surface by dus:Vsalts, fumes, coal dusts, cement dusts, and chemical precipitates from atmosnhere. 0.3 There are various types of silicone compounds, all of which are not suitable as an electrical insulating material for the purpose of prevention of flashover due to pollution. Silicone oil is also not suitable for this purpose. It shall, however, be ensured that the application of the silicone compounds shall not lower the electrical characteristics of the insulators. 0.4 .The hydrocarbon based compounds are also employed for the purpose of prevention of pollution on insulators. 0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : ZThe number of significant places retained in the rounded off value 1960*. should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE

of silicone

1.1 This standard covers the composition, classiikation and requirements corn ounds suitable for application on the surface of high voltage porcelain insJ ators to prevent by their -hydrophobic and encapsulating action the flashover of insulators due to atmospheric pollution. *Rulesfor rounding dfmunaierl

2. TERMXFJOLOGY 2.0 For the purpose of this standard, the following definitions shall apply. 2.1 Softening Point - The temperature at which a substance attains a particular degree of softness under specified conditions of test. 2.2 Arc Resistance - The numerical value of the time in seconds from the start of the test until failure by the formation of a continuous bright line between the electrodes shall be recorded as the measure of the arc resistance of the compound. 3. COMPOSTITON 3.1 Silicone compounds or pastes are compounds of an organo-polysiloxane oil with a reasonably Aat viscosity-temperature curve and incorporating thickners such as graphite, aerosil, inorganic soaps or molybdenum sulphide. The properties of these thickners determine the nature of the silicone compound and consequently the possible uses. All thickners are not suitable for the purpose of prevention of atmospheric pollution. The materials should be homogeneous, smooth in texture and free from lumps and dirts. 4. CLASSIFICATION 4.1 Silicone compounds for application divided into the following two types: on high voltage insulators are

Type A L- In paste or compound form ready to be applied on the cleaned dry insulator by hand or brush. Type B In liquid form, to be applied on the cleaned dry insulator by suitable methods such as spraying or dipping.

5. REQUIREMENTS 5.1 Silicone compounds for application on high voltage insulators shall comply with all the requirements covered in 5.2 and' 5.3 for type A and type B respectively. 5.2 Type A Silicone Compound

5.2.1 General - It shall be transluFen$ vaselinelike consistency, with very high resistance to heat and oxrdatron and very small change in consistency over a wide temperature range. It shall be chemically inert an-d physiologically inert ( nontoxic ), and shall not attack insulators and t&r 4

associated metal fittings. The nontoxicity shall be certified by a recognlsed testing institution. It shall have the following other characteristics: a) Phy.kal charactarirtics Colour. - In its natural form, the colour should be translucent white, light grey or cream. NOTB - A dye or pigment of any colour except black may be added, if required by the user, provided the finished compound meets the other
requirements of this spe&zatibn.

Odour -

6.3 Method for the Determination of Insolubility - About 3 g of the compound, accurately weighed, shall be smeared around the inside of a weighed glass beaker of 250 ml capacity. Approximately 100 ml of the soluticn are enough to immerse the compound and shall be poured into the container. The container shall be tightly capped with metal foil and left to stand for a period of 7 days at a temperature between 22�C and 28�C. At intervals of approximately 24 hours, the solution shall be stirred by moderate manual rotation of the container. At the end of the 7-day period, the solution shall be poured off, and the container and compound rinsed carefully with successive washes of distilIed water until all solvent has been removed. The container and compound shall be dried for 20 hours in an oven at A blank 70�C followed by desiccation for 4 hours over calcium chloride. shall be run to determine the loss due to evaporation which occurs during A final weight less than the original weight of the container the treatment. .and compound shall indicate removal of soluble constituents. Point - Maintain 6.4 Method for the Dete rmination of Solithe material'at a temperature of -60�C for a period of 24 hours. At the end of this period examine the material for any signs of solidification or the material shall not solidify or crack. A slight cracking. At -60�C increase in stiffness of the comnound may be disregarded. 6.5 Test Method for Softening Point -The method described in IS : 12051958* shall be used. The temperature of the compound shall be 200�C for the determination of the softening point. 6.6 Method for the Determination of the Acid Value-The procedure shall be same as given in IS : 1448 [ P : 2 l-1967?. test

APPENDIX ( Clause 9.1 )
SAMPLING FOR TIiR 8ILIGONR

A
COMPOWNDS

A-l.GENERAL REQ~MENT8

OF SAMPLING

A-l.1 Adequate precautions shall be taken to avoid contamination while drawing and transferring samples to suitable, clean, dry and air-tight glass containers. A-l.2 Each sample container after filling shall be sealed air-tight and marked with full identification particulars, such as sample number, the date of sampling, the batch of manufacture of material, and other important particulars of the consignment. 11

Its : 7648 m1975 A-2. SCALE OF SAMPLING

A-2.1 Lot - In a single consignment, all the containers of the same type, size, and drawn from the same batch of manufacture shall constitute a lot. If a consignment is declared or known to consist of different batches of manufacture or of diiferent sizes of containers or of different types of material then the containers belonging to the same batch under the same size and type shall he grouped together and each such group shall constitute a separate lot. ~-2.1.1 Samples shall be tested for each lot for ascertaining conformity of the material to the requirements of the specification. the

A-2.2 The number of containers (n) to be selected from a lot shall depend on the size of the lot (N) and shall be as given in Table 1.
TAELE 1 NUMBER
LOT

OF CONTAINERS
SIZE

TO RE SELECTED

FOR

SAMPLING

x (1) up to 20

NUMBER OF CONTAINERS TOBESELECTED n (2) 3 4 5 6 8 10

21 to 40 41 ,, 80

81 ,, 120 121 ,) 200 201 and above

NOTE - In the case of very small lots where the selection of three containers may be uneconomical, the number of containers to be selected and the criterion for judging the conformity of the lot to the specification shall be as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier.

A-2.3 The containers shall be selected at random and in order to ensure the randomness of selection, a random number table shall be used. In case such a table is not available, the following procedure may be adopted:

Starting from one container; count them in one order as up to r and so on, where r is the integral 1, 2, 3, . ..".................) part of N/n ( N being the lot size and n the number of containers to be selected ). Every rth container thus counted shall be withdrawn to give samples for test.

IS t 7648 - 1973 A-3. PREPARATION SAMPLE OF TEST SAMPLES AND REFERENCE

A-3.1 To ensure that the sample taken from each container is representative of the contents, the contents shall be mixed thoroughly by shaking or by stirring or both. A-3.2 After the contents are thoroughly mixed, a small representative portion of the material shall be taken with the help of a suitable sampling instrument from each of the containers selected. The total quantity of the material drawn from each container shall be sufficient to conduct tests for all requirements as specified in this standard. A-3.3 The material taken equal parts, each forming samples representing n purchaser, another for the sample. from each container shall be divided into three an individual sample. One set of the individual containers selected shall be marked for the supplier and the third to be used as a reference

A-3.4 All the samples shall be transferred to separate containers. These containers shall then be sealed air-tight and labelled with full identification particulars as given in A-1.2. A-3.5 The reference sample consisting of representing n containers selected shall bear and the supplier. They shall be kept at purchaser and the supplier and shall be between the two. A-4. NUMBER OF TESTS a set of tt individual samples the seals of both the purchaser a place agreed to between the used in case of any dispute

A-4.1 Tests for requirements as given in 5.2.1, 5.2.1 (a) and 5.2.1 (b) shall be performed on each of the individual samples taken for this purpose. A-5. CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY

A-5.1 A lot shall be accepted as conforming to this specification if the samples tested meet all the requirements given in 5.2.1, 5.2.1 (a) and 5.2.1 (b).
